newsitem.title: INDIA: Russia, Pakistan may ratify chemical pact - India.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Pakistan may ratify chemical pact - India.

text.p: India said on Monday that it believed both Russia and Pakistan would ratify a treaty banning chemical weapons which went into force earlier this year.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral told Asian News International (ANI) in an interview that he had been told by major powers that Moscow and Islamabad were expected to put aside their objections and ratify the convention.
The convention, which went into effect in April, prohibits the use, development, production and stockpiling of all chemical weapons and provides for their elimination over the next decade.

Russia's parliament resisted international pressure to ratify the treaty, appealing for a significant increase in financial aid and a possible extension of the period for liquidating its chemical arsenals.
The United States, which has ratified the treaty, and Russia are the largest possessors of chemical weapons, with declared stocks of 70,000 tonnes between them.
"As far as Russia is concerned, I am given to understand that Russia has assured other major partners of (the) West that they will do so by September," Gujral said.
"The informal information given to us was that possibly they are putting in place the technology and methodology for destruction because you have to do it gradually," he said.
Gujral noted that Pakistan had also not ratified the chemical weapons treaty. "But again I am told by Americans that perhaps they will do it soon," he said.
India has ratified the convention but refused to sign treaties banning nuclear weapons tests and the manufacture of fissile material used for making nuclear bombs.
